items.stem: Which statements about building a golden record are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Matching links records that refer to the same real-world entity
options.rationale: Correct: matching identifies duplicates across sources.

options.text: Survivorship rules decide which attribute values win in the merged record
options.rationale: Correct: survivorship selects the best value per field.

options.text: A golden record is created by deleting all source records
options.rationale: Sources are usually retained; the golden record is a consolidated view.

options.text: Probabilistic matching requires every field to match exactly
options.rationale: Exact matching is deterministic; probabilistic allows scored, partial matches.

items.stem: Why manage reference data (such as country or currency codes) centrally?

options.text: To keep consistent, versioned code sets that all systems share and map to
options.rationale: Correct: central management avoids divergent, conflicting code lists across systems.

options.text: Because reference data changes many times per second
options.rationale: Reference data is relatively stable, not high-velocity.

options.text: To replace the need for master data entirely
options.rationale: Reference data complements, not replaces, master data.

options.text: Because codes must never be versioned
options.rationale: Versioning with effective dates is a key reference-data practice.

items.explanation: Correct: central management avoids divergent, conflicting code lists across systems.
